anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, the +12V global-label wire is tied to BOTH pin 1 and pin 2 of each fan header (J7 and J8); pin 3 carries the tach signal and pin 4 is marked no-connect (NC). No pin of J7/J8 is connected to GND, so the fan ground return is instead driven to +12V.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists only one 12 V pin per header on the +12V net — 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)' — and standard 4-pin fan wiring (and the open-collector tach pull-up network on the MCU sheet) requires the remaining power pin to be the fan's GND return, not +12V.

evidence.quote: Also on this net: ... and the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2). (Power Architecture, Inputs)

Power sheet (sheet /Power/): +12V label wire runs down with junction dots into J7 pin1 and J7 pin2 and into J8 pin1 and J8 pin2; J7 pin3 / J8 pin3 = FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH; J7 pin4 / J8 pin4 carry NC (no-connect) markers; no GND symbol on either header.

anomalies.impact: A plugged-in fan receives +12V on its ground pin and +12V on its supply pin, so there is no voltage across the motor and no return path: the fans cannot spin, the open-collector tach outputs (referenced to +12V instead of GND) never toggle, the firmware's fan-stall monitoring is defeated, and the oven loses forced-air cooling — an overheat hazard.

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification, but the fan headers J7/J8 have their ground pin (pin 1) tied to the +12V rail instead of GND, leaving no return path for the fans — a deviation from the spec, which places only pin 2 of each header on +12V.
